summary: Sporting News surveys likely destinations for free agent winger Patrick Kane, a 35-year-old three-time Stanley Cup champion rehabbing from hip surgery, as he nears a decision for 2023-24. It weighs the Sabres, Panthers, Red Wings and Stars on fit, cap space, contention and travel. Quotes from Elliotte Friedman inform the analysis, with Detroit and Buffalo looking like the most natural fits.
one_line: Sporting News examines Patrick Kane's free agent options for 2023-24, weighing Buffalo, Florida, Detroit and Dallas on cap space, contention, travel and fit.
key_facts: Patrick Kane is a 35-year-old free agent winger and three-time Stanley Cup champion who has been on the market since the start of the 2023-24 season.

Kane was traded from the Blackhawks to the Rangers at last year's deadline because he wanted another shot at a Cup and not Chicago's rebuild; the Rangers lost in the first round, sending him to free agency for the first time in his career.
Kane had hip surgery over the summer and was expected not to decide until ready to return, so he began the season off an NHL roster.
The Buffalo Sabres have an edge because Kane is a Buffalo native who grew up in the southern part of the city, and they have plenty of cap space.
Entering the final week of November, the Sabres average 2.81 goals per game (eighth-lowest in the NHL) and have a 16.4% power play (23rd); they sit under .500 and sixth in the Atlantic.
About 32% of Kane's career points have come on the power play.

The Florida Panthers are the defending Eastern Conference champions, tied for third in the conference and second in the Atlantic, with about $1.7 million in cap space; Kane could play with center Aleksander Barkov.
Reports say Kane isn't keen on the Western Conference due to travel, but Elliotte Friedman noted Florida and Tampa Bay have the worst travel in the Eastern Conference.
The Detroit Red Wings have the fifth-most cap space in the league and acquired Alex DeBrincat this summer; Kane was DeBrincat's main set-up man when he scored 40 goals a season in Chicago.
Kane called DeBrincat's trade from Chicago to Ottawa "disappointing" and "crushing."
Kane won the Hart Trophy and Art Ross Trophy in 2015-16 while playing with Artemi Panarin in Chicago.
The Dallas Stars are a dark horse: Kane would reportedly love to play there, but they are deep at forward, up against the cap, and per Friedman would rather add on defense.
